**Answer: 5**

I did not verify this by a full derivation. The lower bound of 4 is an argument I can give. The value 5 is recalled from the literature on curves in products of abelian surfaces, not reproduced here.

**Lower bound (genus ≥ 4).** Let $C \subset A_1 \times A_2$ be a non-trivial curve, with normalization still denoted $C$. Since both projections are non-constant, $C$ generates $A_1 \times A_2$. The Albanese map $J(C) \to A_1 \times A_2$ is therefore surjective, so $\dim J(C) = g(C) \ge \dim(A_1\times A_2) = 4$.

**Why the bound is not simply 4.** Equality $g = 4$ would force $J(C)$ to be isogenous to $A_1 \times A_2$. Very general $A_1, A_2$ are non-isogenous simple abelian surfaces of Picard number 1, with no elliptic curves. I did not complete the analysis showing that no genus-4 curve has such a Jacobian, so this step is not proven here.

**Recalled result.** I believe the literature on minimal-genus curves in products of very general abelian surfaces gives 5 as the minimum. This is the value I am reporting.

ANSWER: 5
